_why: A figure image is checked by looking at it. paper/presubmission_check.py requires every image in collect_figures.FIGURE_SOURCES to appear here with the sha256 it currently has; change the image and the gate fails until somebody opens it again. This exists because figure 4 went out with its legend running off the left edge, a paragraph of its caption repeated inside the image, and IORN-006 and IORN-007 printed on its axes, and no computable check could have seen any of it.
_entry: filename -> {sha256, reviewed (ISO date), by, note}. Record what was seen, not that it was opened. An image with a known defect does not belong here: leave it out and let the gate stay red until it is redrawn.
_hashes_are_environment_specific: A PNG's bytes depend on the matplotlib and freetype that drew it, so regenerating the figures in a different environment changes every hash here even when nothing about the figures changed. Verified on 2026-10-21: a clean archive in a fresh virtual environment redrew all four generated figures to different digests. That is the intended behaviour of this ledger locally -- a library upgrade is a reason to look again -- but it means a reader who installs the archive and redraws the figures will see this check fail, and that is not a defect in the release. The data availability statement promises the frozen result tables and the commands that regenerate the figures, not that an author's review ledger still matches.

_what_was_wrong_before.figure4_scatter.png: As first submitted: the legend ran off the left edge of the canvas with its three entries cut mid-word, the legend overlapped the plot, a four-line paragraph was drawn inside the image repeating what the caption already said, and both axis titles carried this programme's internal identifiers, 'IORN-006 organ-weighted CTDIvol' and 'IORN-007 absorbed organ dose'. Fixed 2026-10-21 in tools/figure4_scatter.py.
_what_was_wrong_before.figure6_vendor.png: As first submitted: the image had 'Figure 5  Scan-covering organ dose by vendor' drawn across the top, because the pipeline numbered it 5 and collect_figures renamed the file to 6 without repainting it, so the manuscript printed Figure 5 above the image and Figure 6 in the caption below. Fixed 2026-10-21 in tools/collect_phase2_results.py; the source file is now vendor_organ_dose.png and carries no number.

_drawn_on: The environment the digests above were produced in. A PNG's bytes depend on the matplotlib and freetype that drew it, so this is what tells check_every_figure_image_has_been_looked_at whether a mismatch means a figure changed or only that it is being checked somewhere else.

figure1_ladder.png.by: Claude Opus 5, on the author's instruction
figure1_ladder.png.note: New. Three panels on one axial abdominal section: (a) the recorded CTDIvol over the whole examination, (b) the organ-weighted index painted on ten segmented organs, (c) absorbed organ dose on the same organs, (b) and (c) sharing one colour scale and one colourbar. Looked at: the two overlays have identical geometry, as they must, and differ only in colour; (b) reads almost uniform and (c) does not, which is the result the paper reports and not a drawing fault; organ names are printed on (b) alone and none of the five overlaps another or leaves the panel; the arrows sit in the gaps and touch nothing; the colourbar spans (b) and (c) only, which is correct because (a) carries no per-organ value; the credit line and acquisition sit under (a) in the space the colourbar leaves; no figure number and no caption text is drawn inside the image; nearest-neighbour throughout, so no interpolation colour appears at an organ boundary. Redrawn with the organ names and the credit line at 7 pt, because 6 pt is below what a journal accepts and below what paper/make_figures.py's own docstring promises; looked at again at that size and every label is legible and none has moved onto a neighbour. 6.50 x 2.40 in, inside the text block.

figure6_conversion_ceiling.png.by: Claude Opus 5, on the author's instruction
figure6_conversion_ceiling.png.note: Redrawn 2026-11-07, both panels. (a) now scores the error against the Monte-Carlo dose rather than against the model's own prediction, so the first two rows read 29 % and 28 % and the per-organ row is the shorter of the two; the ordering of the five rows is unchanged below them. (b) used to draw patients, organs and vendors as three bars of one whole, which they are not: every patient here contributed one series and therefore one scanner, so the vendor bar was a slice of the patient bar standing beside it. It now has five bars in two groups separated by a rule -- above it the marginal shares with the vendor bar drawn thinner, lighter and labelled '(of which, vendor)' directly under 'Between patients'; below it 'Patient and organ, fitted' at 94 % and 'Residual' at 6 %, the pair that sums to one. Looked at: every row label is inside the canvas and none collides with a bar or its value label; the 4 % vendor bar is short but its label is clear of the axis; the rule at y = 2.5 sits in the gap between 'Between organs' and 'Patient and organ, fitted' and touches no bar; the 94 % bar does not run past the axis; both panel titles and both axis titles are present; no figure number and no caption text is drawn inside the image. The two panels keep the same widths and the figure is 6.50 x 3.40 in, inside the text block.
